core_obligations: Translate into extensions (proof lines 8949-8954): by the companion lemma the first cohomology group is the vector space of extensions of the trivial module by the given module.

Encode an extension by finitely many vectors (proof lines 8955-8966): choosing topological generators of the group and a lift of the generator of the quotient, the elements obtained by applying the generators to that lift determine the isomorphism class of the extension; hence the space of extensions is a subquotient of a finite power of the module, which the author records as routine.

Show the vectors determine the extension completely (proof lines 8967-8975): continuity provides an open subgroup acting trivially on the chosen lift, every coset of that subgroup contains a word in the chosen generators, and since the effect of a word is determined by the finitely many vectors, so is the effect of an arbitrary group element.
proof_roadmap: Identify the first cohomology with a space of extensions of the trivial module.
Choose topological generators and a lift, and attach to each extension finitely many vectors of the module.
Show that those vectors determine the extension, so that the extension space sits inside a finite power of a finite dimensional space.
difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the first cohomology of a finite dimensional continuous module over a topologically finitely generated group: it is finite dimensional (statement lines 8940-8946). The proof is a complete argument: the companion lemma identifies the group with a space of extensions (proof lines 8949-8954); choosing topological generators and a lift of the generator of the quotient attaches to each extension finitely many vectors of the module, so that the extension space is a subquotient of a finite power of a finite dimensional vector space (proof lines 8955-8966); and continuity together with the density of the subgroup generated by the chosen elements shows that those vectors determine the extension, completing the argument (proof lines 8967-8975). The non-formal content is the encoding of an extension by finitely many vectors. The claim is H2: a structured reduction with the continuity input used explicitly.
